answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock a stake at a shared wharf of escrow before joining the market, and the stake is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Newcomers start with low trust and gain limits only through verified work over time, so a flood of fake agents faces a gale of rising costs rather than free entry. Attackers who try to spiral cheap identities into influence must fund every one, and the escrow burns their stake when fraud is proven, turning mass identity creation from a cheap trick into a losing trade.
